qc_lac_long.blurb: Lac Long is a cliff-and-lake climbing site in the Portneuf region of Quebec, near Saint-Alban, about an hour and a half from Quebec City. The cliffs stand across a lake and a stream, reached by bridges, and are split into eighteen numbered sectors plus a small bouldering zone. Climbing leans traditional, with bolts mostly appearing where gear will not fit, so expect trad and mixed routes alongside a good number of sport lines. It suits leaders comfortable at 5.10 and up: the largest group sits at 5.10 and 5.11, with a smaller spread of 5.12, a few 5.13s and fewer easy routes. The cliff is sunny. Larger sectors include La Croisée des Chemins, l'Arène, La Cour and Le Cosmodrome.

id_teddy_bear_cove.blurb: Teddy Bear Cove is a sport-climbing area in East Idaho, a few miles from Massacre Rocks, where sand dunes and prairie meet the tops of the basalt cliffs. The basalt comes from overlapping lava flows, so the rock is steeper and more roofed than at its neighbour, with big moves on big holds and some loose, blocky bands between flows. Nearly every route is bolted and short, so a rope and draws is nearly all you need. Most climbs are 5.10 and 5.11, with a fair number of 5.9 and 5.12 and only a few easier or at 5.13. Walls such as The Pit and Juniper Wall, Send Town and The Nose hold the most routes. Sun-baked alcoves make it a standout winter spot, and it can be climbed year-round.

nm_las_conchas.blurb: Las Conchas is a sport-climbing area in the Jemez Mountains of northern New Mexico, between Valles Caldera and Bandelier and a bit under two hours from Albuquerque. The crags sit in meadows and spruce forest, many along the East Fork of the Jemez River. Sport routes dominate, backed by a few trad lines and about twenty boulder problems from V0 to V5. Routes cluster between 5.10 and 5.12, with a fair number of 5.9 and below and a few 5.13s. The elevation keeps summer days fairly cool, and it can be climbed year-round: the south-facing walls of Retirement Wall, Hidden Tower and Easy Bake Alcove are sheltered and pleasant on sunny, calm winter days. Cattle Call Wall is the most visible cliff from the meadow.

wv_beauty_mountain.blurb: Beauty Mountain is a sector of the New River Gorge in West Virginia, reached by a gravel road that drops down into the gorge. Bouldering makes up nearly half of the climbs, with sport and trad roughly equal beside it. Roped climbs run from 5.7 to 5.14, weighted toward 5.10 through 5.13, so it suits stronger climbers more than beginners. Notable roped walls include The Brain, Burning Buttress and Thunder Buttress. Bouldering centres on Short Creek, a collection of boulders around and below the cliffline that steps down toward the gorge along the creek, with problems from V0 to V10.

ca_santa_monica_mountains_bouldering.blurb: Santa Monica Mountains Bouldering covers the boulder spots of the Santa Monica Mountains in the Los Angeles area. Its two largest sets are the Malibu Tunnel Boulders, water-polished sandstone blocks along a creek beside the canyon road, and Purple Stones, a canyon site near Topanga where soft sandstone turns brittle after rain. Smaller clusters such as Miniholland and Gainsborough Boulders add more. Nearly all of it is bouldering, with a couple of top-ropes. Most problems are V0 to V4, with a solid group at V5 and V6 and a hard tail reaching V10. Creekside approaches are brushy with heavy poison oak, and the rock needs several days to dry after rain.

mt_eastside_of_the_reservoir.blurb: The east side of Koocanusa Reservoir holds the biggest share of the Stone Hill climbing, on bluffs above the lake in northwest Montana. Stone Hill’s rock is extremely hard quartzite, giving sharp edges, thin cracks, steep slabs and small roofs, so footwork and crimping matter as much as jamming. Sport leads over trad, with a handful of boulder problems, and routes run from 5.5 to 5.13 with a heavy middle at 5.10, a good number of 5.8 and 5.9, and a thinner top end in 5.12 and 5.13. Hold Up Bluffs is the largest sector, followed by South Stone and Peck Gulch. Approaches tend to be shorter than the crags are tall, and across Stone Hill the sunny walls dry out early in spring.
